hints.junior: Layout, Sidebar, and UserPanel don't render anything about the user — they just take the prop in and immediately hand it back out.
hints.mid: Prop drilling isn't a correctness bug, it's a maintenance tax — every new deep prop means editing every intermediate component's signature.
hints.staff: The real cost is coupling: components that have zero logic depending on a value still carry it in their prop types, and refactoring them risks breaking a data path they don't participate in.

hints.junior: Click Ship in each mode and watch which components light up as edited.
hints.mid: Prop drilling ripples the new prop through every intermediate signature. Composition only changes the owner and the consumer.
hints.staff: The files-touched count is the concrete, measurable difference — same visual feature, a different number of contracts that had to change.

hints.junior: Pass the already-built child element down as children instead of the raw data — the components in between never need to know the data exists.
hints.mid: The owner builds the deep child directly and hands it down as children; intermediate components just render {children} wherever it belongs.
hints.staff: This fits one-owner, one-consumer data through structural components — it's the wrong tool when the same data is needed at many scattered points, that's a Context problem instead.

hints.junior: One or two levels of prop passing isn't a real problem — the pain starts around three or more untouched layers.
hints.mid: Context is for data needed at many scattered points; composing it through every leaf that happens to want it just relocates the same coupling.
hints.staff: Composition has no re-render fan-out the way Context does — it's plain JSX passed as a prop, not a shared subscription every consumer re-renders on.

sections.junior: Today's case is about a user prop that had to pass through three components that never actually use it, just to reach an avatar five levels down.
sections.mid: Prop drilling couples every intermediate component to a prop it only ever forwards, and that coupling compounds every time a new piece of deep data needs the same path.
sections.staff: The real cost isn't the extra typing, it's that components end up carrying values in their signatures that have nothing to do with what they actually render.

sections.junior: Instead of forwarding the raw user data through every layout component, the component that owns the data builds the deep child itself and passes that finished piece down as children.
sections.mid: The owner composes the tree top down, handing already-built elements to the layout components, which just render whatever was passed to them.
sections.staff: This is composition doing the job people often reach for prop drilling, or prematurely, context, to solve — it fits one owner flowing to one consumer, not data that's scattered across many unrelated points.

sections.junior: Ship the same feature in both modes and watch which component cards flash as edited versus which stay untouched.
sections.mid: In prop drilling mode every layout component's signature changes. In composition mode only the top and bottom of the chain change.
sections.staff: Watch the files-touched count at the bottom — that's a direct, countable measure of how much surface area each approach exposes to a small feature change.

sections.junior: If a component only takes a prop to hand it straight to a child, pass the already-built child down instead so the middle never needs that prop.
sections.mid: Compose from the top: the data's owner builds the deep consumer and hands it down as children, so layout components only ever describe layout.
sections.staff: Composition suits one-owner-one-consumer data flowing through structural components. Data needed at many scattered points across the tree calls for context instead, not composition.
